title: Lesson 13 · The Verb in Depth I
blurb: Voice (active/passive), the five modes, the six tenses, subject-verb agreement, and verb properties.

items.prompt:
Is the verb active (subject acts) or passive (subject is acted upon)?

“The boy wrote a letter.”
items.explain: The boy does the writing — active voice.

items.prompt:
Is the verb active (subject acts) or passive (subject is acted upon)?

“The letter was written.”
items.explain: The letter receives the action — passive voice.

items.prompt:
Is the verb active (subject acts) or passive (subject is acted upon)?

“The dog chased the cat.”
items.explain: The dog does the chasing — active voice.

items.prompt:
Is the verb active (subject acts) or passive (subject is acted upon)?

“The cat was chased.”
items.explain: The cat receives the action — passive voice.

items.prompt:
Is the verb active (subject acts) or passive (subject is acted upon)?

“Columbus discovered America.”
items.explain: Columbus does the discovering — active voice.

items.prompt:
Is the verb active (subject acts) or passive (subject is acted upon)?

“America was discovered.”
items.explain: America receives the action — passive voice.

items.prompt:
Is the verb active (subject acts) or passive (subject is acted upon)?

“The mail was robbed.”
items.explain: The mail receives the action — passive voice.

items.prompt:
Is the verb active (subject acts) or passive (subject is acted upon)?

“Farmers plant corn.”
items.explain: The farmers do the planting — active voice.

items.prompt:
What mode is the verb “burns”?

“Fire burns.”
items.explain: It states a fact — indicative mode.

items.prompt:
What mode is the verb “must go”?

“You must go.”
items.explain: “must” tells of necessity — potential mode.

items.prompt:
What mode is the verb “Go”?

“Go home.”
items.explain: It gives a command — imperative mode.

items.prompt:
What mode is the verb “be”?

“If it be true, I will come.”
items.explain: It states a supposition with “if” — subjunctive mode.

items.prompt:
What mode is the verb “to play”?

“He wants to play.”
items.explain: “to play” names the action without affirming it — infinitive mode.

items.prompt:
What mode is the verb “can sing”?

“She can sing.”
items.explain: “can” tells of power or ability — potential mode.

items.prompt:
What mode is the verb “encamped”?

“The army encamped.”
items.explain: It states a fact — indicative mode.

items.prompt:
What mode is the verb “Lift”?

“Lift up your heads.”
items.explain: It gives a command — imperative mode.

items.prompt:
What tense is the verb?

“I write.”
items.explain: The action is now — present tense.

items.prompt:
What tense is the verb?

“I wrote.”
items.explain: The action was before now — past tense.

items.prompt:
What tense is the verb?

“I shall write.”
items.explain: The action is to come — future tense.

items.prompt:
What tense is the verb?

“I have written.”
items.explain: Past action linked to now — present perfect tense.

items.prompt:
What tense is the verb?

“I had written.”
items.explain: Action before another past time — past perfect tense.

items.prompt:
What tense is the verb?

“I shall have written.”
items.explain: Action to be finished before a future point — future perfect tense.

items.prompt:
What tense is the verb?

“The wind blows.”
items.explain: The action is now — present tense.

items.prompt:
What tense is the verb?

“The bridge had fallen.”
items.explain: Action before another past time — past perfect tense.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“The boy ___ fast.”
items.explain: A singular subject takes a singular verb: the boy runs.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“The boys ___ fast.”
items.explain: A plural subject takes a plural verb: the boys run.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“She ___ letters.”
items.explain: A singular subject takes a singular verb: she writes.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“They ___ here.”
items.explain: A plural subject takes a plural verb: they were.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“He ___ his work.”
items.explain: A singular subject takes a singular verb: he does.

items.prompt:
Choose the verb that agrees with the subject:

“The dogs ___ loudly.”
items.explain: A plural subject takes a plural verb: the dogs bark.

items.prompt: Voice belongs to which verbs?
items.explain: Only transitive verbs have voice — they can act or be acted upon.

items.prompt: How many tenses are there?
items.explain: There are six tenses.

items.prompt: How many modes are there?
items.explain: There are five modes: indicative, potential, subjunctive, imperative, infinitive.

items.prompt: A verb must agree with its subject in what?
items.explain: A verb agrees with its subject in person and number.
